newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian minister regrets U.S. election comment.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian minister regrets U.S. election comment.

text.p: Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said on Tuesday he regretted a U.S. State Department statement that last week's general elections were tightly controlled, the official Antara news agency reported.

State Department spokesman John Dinger said in Washington last Friday the United States wanted to see changes in Indonesia's political system and believed that parliamentary elections were tightly controlled by the government.
"I regret the statement," Antara quoted Alatas as telling reporters, adding that other countries had yet to understand that Indonesia had its own form of democracy.
"I just hope that there is a willingness by other countries to understand...that we have a different form of democracy," he said.
Indonesia's ruling Golkar, in power for most of President Suharto's 30-year rule, won a record 74 percent of the votes in last Thursday's national and local elections held every five years.

Of the two other parties legally entitled to contest the poll, the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) took nearly 23 percent of the vote, while the Christian-Nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) had three percent.
Dinger said the electoral system severely limited political competition and Indonesian citizens did not have the ability to change their government through democratic means.
Independent monitors and the PPP said they had found widespread irregularities during the election.
